summary: Skoda's compact electric SUV undercuts every other European EV on price in Australia and reviewers consistently rate its efficiency and conventional, button-rich cabin highly. The split verdict is on ride and range: Australian testers find the fixed-rate suspension too firm for patchy suburban tarmac, and for MY27 the entry 60 Select moves to a 58kWh usable LFP pack with 406km WLTP and slower 105kW DC charging, so touring buyers pay $7,000 more for the 85 Select's 521km and 165kW. Only the two Select grades are orderable: the Sportline 85 is announced but orders do not open until early 2027, and cheap prepaid servicing and a seven-year warranty offset an equipment list that still omits surround-view cameras and a connected app.
pros: 60 Select lists at $48,990 before on-roads (Skoda advertises $49,990 drive-away to 31/12/26), making it the cheapest European-built EV on sale in Australia and priced against Chinese rivals like the BYD Atto 3 and Geely EX5
Genuinely efficient: CarsGuide's long-term MY26 60 Select averaged 15.9kWh/100km, exactly matching that car's WLTP claim, and CarExpert saw 12.8kWh/100km in the 85
The 85 Select charges at up to 165kW DC, 10-80 per cent in about 29 minutes, and carries a 77kWh usable pack for 521km WLTP
Prepaid servicing works out to roughly $195 a year over 10 years, with a 7-year/unlimited-km warranty
Rear-drive chassis, 9.3m turning circle and retained physical climate controls; 470L boot expanding to 1580L with Skoda's usual clever storage
cons: Suspension is tuned too firmly for Australian roads - reviewers report a busy, thumping ride over road joins, and no adaptive dampers are offered on Select grades
MY27 60 Select's LFP pack holds 58kWh usable for 406km WLTP and peaks at only 105kW DC (10-80 per cent in about 26 minutes), so genuine touring range means paying $7,000 more for the 85 Select
No ANCAP rating as at July 2026 - it relies on a 2025 five-star Euro NCAP result, which can be a blocker for fleet and novated-lease policies
Select grades go without surround-view camera, vehicle-to-load and a spare tyre, and Skoda Australia does not offer the embedded connectivity and app store sold overseas
Lane-keeping assistance is over-sensitive and needs resetting each drive, a common complaint across Australian first drives
